title: Reminder reliability: inexact alarms and stale-alarm cleanup
boundary: **Not in this slice:** the receiver reading fresh data, skipping satisfied trackers and time-change broadcasts (S36), tap-to-open (S37), the notification icon (S12), and the "Mark done" action (a later item).

sections.heading: Why
sections.body:
- The owner decided to drop exact alarms. `SCHEDULE_EXACT_ALARM` is a special-access permission that habit reminders do not need, and Google Play scrutinizes it.
- `importBackup` deletes all trackers and re-inserts them with new ids. `rescheduleReminders` only schedules the new ids, so alarms for the old ids (the `PendingIntent` request code is the tracker id) stay armed and fire with stale names.

sections.heading: Failing tests
sections.body: - None practical: the work is `AlarmManager` calls. The Check section verifies with `dumpsys alarm`. The pure scheduling-time logic is already covered by S02's `nextReminderTrigger` tests, which must keep passing.

sections.heading: Implement
sections.body:
1. Remove the `SCHEDULE_EXACT_ALARM` permission and its comment from the manifest. In `ReminderScheduler`, delete `canScheduleExactAlarms()`, the exact branch and the `@SuppressLint("ScheduleExactAlarm")`. Always call `alarmManager.setAndAllowWhileIdle(RTC_WAKEUP, triggerAt, pendingIntent)`.
2. Add `fun cancelAll(ids: Collection<Long>) = ids.forEach(::cancelTracker)` to `ReminderScheduler`.
3. In `TrackerViewModel.importBackup`: before running the import, read the existing tracker ids with `repository.getReminderBundles().map { it.tracker.id }` and call `reminderScheduler.cancelAll(ids)`. On success call `rescheduleReminders()` as today. On failure, also call `rescheduleReminders()` so the previous trackers' reminders are re-armed (the database is unchanged when the import fails).
4. Archiving already cancels the alarm (`archiveTracker` in the ViewModel). S15 adds the same for permanent delete.
5. In `DEVELOPERS.md` (a new "Reminders" section), state that reminders use inexact alarms (`setAndAllowWhileIdle`) and may arrive late, especially in Doze, and give the maximum delay you measured in the Check section (for example "up to N minutes on Android 14, M minutes on Android 8 in our tests"). Do not write a figure you did not measure.

sections.heading: Check
sections.body:
- `./gradlew testDebugUnitTest lintDebug assembleDebug` passes, including S02's reminder tests.
- The merged manifest has no `SCHEDULE_EXACT_ALARM`: `aapt dump permissions app/build/outputs/apk/debug/app-debug.apk` lists only `POST_NOTIFICATIONS` and `RECEIVE_BOOT_COMPLETED`.
- Manual, on a device or emulator: create two trackers with reminders and run `adb shell dumpsys alarm | grep -c com.squalor.consecutor` to see the armed alarms. Import a backup that has different trackers and run it again: only the imported trackers' alarms remain.
- A reminder set 2 minutes ahead is delivered.
- Measure the delivery window. On an API 26 and an API 34 emulator, create a reminder about 12 hours ahead, then run `adb shell dumpsys alarm` and find the app's alarm. Record `whenElapsed` and `maxWhenElapsed` (the latest time the system may deliver it); the difference is the window. Record both values with `slicer note S08` and use them in the `DEVELOPERS.md` text. If either window is more than one hour, say so in the note and leave the scheduling as it is: changing the strategy is an owner decision.
